3. Plaintiff's case in brief, that his father late Raj Behari Mondal was owner and possessor of the suit land including other lands. He and his deceased brother Avimannya were two sons of Raj Behari Mondal. During lifetime of their father, Avimannya died on 12-8-1958 leaving behind him, father Raj Behari Mondal, their mother Samela Bala Mondal, wife Gouri Dasi, and two daughters. Avimannaya has no son. Raj Behari Mondal died at the age near about 100 years in Salt Lake, Kolkata, wherein they took shelter during the liberation war leaving behind one son the plaintiff, his wife (plaintiff's mother the defendant No.2), and the defendant No.1 Gouri Dasi (widow of deceased Avimannya) According to Daybhaga School of Hindu Law he (plaintiff) is the sole successor in the properties left by his father. Raj Behari Mondal had no other son, grandson, or grand grandson. As such since after their return from India in March 1972 he has been enjoying and possessing the entire property left by his father, and except him nobody has or can claim any right, title and possession over such property. The SA records in respect of the suit land were correctly prepared and finally published in his father's name who had been in enjoyment and possession, and had been paying rent and taxes till the liberation war in 1971. That on 5th Agrahayan 1389 BS he came to know that the defendant No.1 Gouri Dasi Mondal being advised by some evil mongers made an application before the Circle Officer (Revenue), Batiaghata for mutation of 5.95 acres of the suit land in her name, and accordingly 5.95 acres of land was mutated in her name. On 17-1-1983 after obtaining copies of the application made by the defendant No.1 and the order passed thereon from the office of the Circle Officer (Revenue) he became sure about such mutation. The defendant No.1 Gouri Dasi is not entitle to get any Agricultural Land left by Raj Behari Mondal since her husband died during lifetime of his father having no son. As such the order of mutation passed by the Circle Officer (Revenue) is illegal, and not binding upon him. Being asked by him on 20-1-1983 the defendant No.1 replied that the Circle Officer (Revenue) said her that, even after death of her husband during his father's lifetime she will get 50% of the property left her father-in-law. She threatened him that in case of objection in taking possession of such property she will sale the same to any mighty person. The defendants have no right, title and possession over the suit land since they are not entitle to get the same. He is the only successor in the suit land left by his father. The suit land is Agricultural Land and the defendants cannot claim any right, title possession over the same. Hence, to avoid future complications, instituted the suit. 

 24. To decide the question whether the defendant Gouri Dasi is entitle to inherit the Agricultural Land as she claims the concern law required to followed is "The Hindu Women's Right to Property Act, 1937 (Act No. XVIII of 1937)" which was subsequently amended by "The Hindu Women's Rights to Property (Amendment) Act, 1938, (Act No. II of 1938)". The said Act was enacted on 14th April, 1937 in the then British India. The statements of object and reason to enact such law had been published in the Gazette of India, 1935, Part V, Page-131.
